title: Ethiopian English University Entrance Practice Test 14 2024
description: Ethiopian English University Entrance Practice Test 14 2024 featuring 100 authentic questions with step-by-step solutions. Designed for Ethiopian national exam mastery.

questions.questionText: There was ___ information available about the incident, so the investigators had to continue searching.
questions.explanation: Information is uncountable, and little expresses an insufficient amount.

questions.questionText: ___ of the students who applied for the scholarship were selected, so competition was extremely high.
questions.explanation: Students is plural countable, and few expresses a small, insufficient number.

questions.questionText: The number of applicants ___ increased significantly this year.
questions.explanation: The number of takes a singular verb.

questions.questionText: A number of applicants ___ still waiting outside the examination hall.
questions.explanation: A number of means several or many and takes a plural verb.

questions.questionText: There isn't ___ evidence to support the accusation.
questions.explanation: Evidence is uncountable, so much is appropriate.

questions.questionText: The researcher collected ___ pieces of evidence before reaching a conclusion.
questions.explanation: Pieces is plural countable, so several is appropriate.

questions.questionText: There are ___ students in the laboratory that several of them have to work outside.
questions.explanation: Students is plural countable, so too many is required.

questions.questionText: The laboratory contains ___ equipment for such a small research team.
questions.explanation: Equipment is uncountable, so too much is correct.

questions.questionText: We have ___ time left, so we must finish the experiment immediately.
questions.explanation: Time is uncountable, and little emphasizes an insufficient amount.

questions.questionText: We have ___ time left, so there is no need to hurry.
questions.explanation: A little means a small amount that is available and may be sufficient.

questions.questionText: Only ___ candidates managed to solve the final problem correctly.
questions.explanation: Candidates is plural countable, so a few is correct.

questions.questionText: ___ candidates managed to solve the final problem, which surprised the examiners.
questions.explanation: Few emphasizes that almost none succeeded.

questions.questionText: Would you like ___ coffee before the meeting begins?
questions.explanation: Some is commonly used in offers when a positive response is expected.

questions.questionText: I don't have ___ money with me today.
questions.explanation: Any is commonly used in negative sentences with uncountable nouns.

questions.questionText: Do you have ___ useful information about the new admission requirements?
questions.explanation: Any is normally used in questions with uncountable information.

questions.questionText: Could I have ___ water before the examination starts?
questions.explanation: Some is appropriate in a request when a positive response is expected.

questions.questionText: You may select ___ book from the shelf for your research.
questions.explanation: In an affirmative sentence, any can mean it does not matter which one.

questions.questionText: There are ___ books on the subject, but none deals specifically with this problem.
questions.explanation: Books is plural countable, so several is correct.

questions.questionText: The professor gave us ___ useful advice before the examination.
questions.explanation: Advice is uncountable, and a lot of works with uncountable nouns.

questions.questionText: There were ___ mistakes in his first draft, so he had to rewrite most of it.
questions.explanation: Mistakes is plural countable, so a lot of is appropriate.

questions.questionText: The lecturer provided ___ detailed explanations that the students understood the topic immediately.
questions.explanation: Explanations is plural countable, so so many is correct.

questions.questionText: The lecturer provided ___ information that the students struggled to remember it all.
questions.explanation: Information is uncountable, so so much is required.

questions.questionText: There were ___ applicants that the university had to extend the selection process.
questions.explanation: Applicants is plural countable, so so many is correct.

questions.questionText: He spent ___ money on unnecessary equipment and eventually ran out of funds.
questions.explanation: Money is uncountable, so too much is correct.

questions.questionText: She made ___ errors in the calculation that the final answer was completely unreliable.
questions.explanation: Errors is plural countable, so too many is correct.

questions.questionText: The students had ___ opportunities to practice, so most of them remained unprepared.
questions.explanation: Few emphasizes an insufficient number of opportunities.

questions.questionText: The students had ___ opportunities to practice, which helped them prepare adequately.
questions.explanation: A few means some opportunities existed and were useful.

questions.questionText: There is ___ hope of completing the project today unless additional workers arrive.
questions.explanation: Hope is uncountable in this meaning, and little expresses an insufficient amount.

questions.questionText: There is ___ hope left, so we should not give up yet.
questions.explanation: A little indicates that some hope remains.

questions.questionText: ___ of the information in the report was verified independently.
questions.explanation: None is used without a noun after it and can refer to an uncountable amount.

questions.questionText: There was ___ information in the report that could be verified independently.
questions.explanation: No is placed directly before a noun.

questions.questionText: ___ of the students submitted their assignments before the deadline.
questions.explanation: None of is used before a plural noun phrase.

questions.questionText: ___ students submitted their assignments before the deadline.
questions.explanation: No is used directly before the plural noun students.

questions.questionText: ___ of the money collected was used for administrative expenses.
questions.explanation: All can refer to the whole amount of an uncountable noun.

questions.questionText: ___ of the students in the final group received certificates.
questions.explanation: All of can refer to the whole group.

questions.questionText: ___ of my brothers has a different area of specialization.
questions.explanation: Each of is followed by a plural noun phrase and emphasizes individuals.

questions.questionText: ___ student in the advanced class must submit an individual research proposal.
questions.explanation: Every is followed directly by a singular countable noun.

questions.questionText: ___ of the two candidates was given an opportunity to defend the proposal.
questions.explanation: Each of can refer to two or more individuals separately.

questions.questionText: ___ candidates were qualified, but only one was selected.
questions.explanation: Both specifically refers to two candidates.

questions.questionText: ___ of the two proposals has serious weaknesses.
questions.explanation: Each of can refer to two proposals individually.

questions.questionText: ___ student has to bring a valid identification card.
questions.explanation: Every is followed directly by a singular countable noun.

questions.questionText: ___ of the students has submitted the required document.
questions.explanation: Each can be followed by of + plural noun and takes a singular verb.

questions.questionText: The number of students applying for engineering ___ rising rapidly.
questions.explanation: The number of refers to one total and takes a singular verb.

questions.questionText: A number of students ___ requested additional preparation materials.
questions.explanation: A number of means several and takes a plural verb.

questions.questionText: There is ___ furniture in the new classroom, but more desks are needed.
questions.explanation: Furniture is uncountable, so a little is correct.

questions.questionText: There are ___ pieces of furniture in the storage room.
questions.explanation: Pieces is plural countable, so several is correct.

questions.questionText: The university has ___ accommodation available for international students.
questions.explanation: Accommodation is uncountable, so a lot of is appropriate.

questions.questionText: The university has ___ rooms available for international students.
questions.explanation: Rooms is plural countable, and a lot of works with plural countable nouns.

questions.questionText: The committee received ___ applications than expected.
questions.explanation: Applications is plural countable, so many is appropriate.

questions.questionText: The committee received ___ information than expected.
questions.explanation: Information is uncountable, so much is correct.

questions.questionText: There isn't ___ rice left to feed all the guests.
questions.explanation: Rice is uncountable, so much is correct.

questions.questionText: There aren't ___ plates left for all the guests.
questions.explanation: Plates is plural countable, so many is required.

questions.questionText: She has ___ knowledge of the subject, but not enough to teach it.
questions.explanation: Knowledge is uncountable, and little indicates an insufficient amount.

questions.questionText: She has ___ knowledge of the subject and can answer most basic questions.
questions.explanation: A little indicates that some knowledge is available.

questions.questionText: There were ___ people at the meeting, so the hall looked almost empty.
questions.explanation: Few means a small and insufficient number.

questions.questionText: There were ___ people at the meeting, enough to form a useful discussion.
questions.explanation: A few means some people were present.

questions.questionText: The teacher gave the students ___ homework that they needed the entire weekend to complete it.
questions.explanation: Homework is uncountable, so so much is correct.

questions.questionText: The teacher assigned ___ exercises that the students could not finish them in one evening.
questions.explanation: Exercises is plural countable, so so many is correct.

questions.questionText: There was ___ traffic on the road that we arrived an hour late.
questions.explanation: Traffic is uncountable, so so much is correct.

questions.questionText: There were ___ vehicles on the road that traffic came to a complete standstill.
questions.explanation: Vehicles is plural countable, so so many is correct.

questions.questionText: We have ___ food for everyone, so there is no need to order more.
questions.explanation: Enough means as much as necessary.

questions.questionText: There are ___ chairs for everyone in the room.
questions.explanation: Enough can be used with plural countable nouns.

questions.questionText: The candidate was not experienced ___ to handle the investigation alone.
questions.explanation: With adjectives, enough follows the adjective.

questions.questionText: She did not speak clearly ___ for everyone at the back to hear her.
questions.explanation: Enough follows an adverb such as clearly.

questions.questionText: We have ___ resources to complete the project without additional funding.
questions.explanation: Plenty of means more than enough and works with plural countable nouns.

questions.questionText: There is ___ water in the reservoir to supply the town for several months.
questions.explanation: Plenty of works with uncountable nouns and indicates abundance.

questions.questionText: ___ of the two explanations fully accounts for the unexpected result.
questions.explanation: Both refers to two people or things together.

questions.questionText: ___ of the evidence was sufficient to prove the claim.
questions.explanation: None can refer to an uncountable amount.

questions.questionText: ___ of the students in the group completed the assignment, although some submitted it late.
questions.explanation: All refers to the whole plural group.

questions.questionText: ___ student in the class was given a separate answer sheet.
questions.explanation: Every is followed by a singular countable noun.

questions.questionText: ___ of the participants received individual feedback.
questions.explanation: Each of is followed by a plural noun and emphasizes individuals.

questions.questionText: ___ participants received individual feedback.
questions.explanation: All can directly modify a plural countable noun.

questions.questionText: There are ___ reasons why the proposal should be reconsidered.
questions.explanation: Reasons is plural countable, so several is appropriate.

questions.questionText: There is ___ reason to believe that the results were manipulated.
questions.explanation: Reason is singular countable, and some can modify a singular countable noun in this meaning.

questions.questionText: I need ___ more information before I can make a final decision.
questions.explanation: Information is uncountable, and some is appropriate in an affirmative sentence.

questions.questionText: The report contains ___ useful information, but it does not answer the main question.
questions.explanation: Information is uncountable, so some is appropriate.

questions.questionText: We did not receive ___ useful information from the interview.
questions.explanation: Any is normally used in negative sentences.

questions.questionText: How ___ money will be required to complete the construction?
questions.explanation: Money is uncountable, so how much is required.

questions.questionText: How ___ applicants were invited to the second interview?
questions.explanation: Applicants is plural countable, so how many is correct.

questions.questionText: There is not ___ room in the laboratory for another large machine.
questions.explanation: Room is uncountable in this meaning, so much is correct.

questions.questionText: There are not ___ spaces available in the laboratory.
questions.explanation: Spaces is plural countable, so many is correct.

questions.questionText: The committee has ___ money remaining, but it is enough to finish the project.
questions.explanation: A little indicates a small amount that is nevertheless available.

questions.questionText: The committee has ___ money remaining, so the project will probably be cancelled.
questions.explanation: Little emphasizes an insufficient amount.

questions.questionText: The university offers ___ opportunities for students to conduct research.
questions.explanation: Opportunities is plural countable, and plenty of indicates abundance.

questions.questionText: The university provides ___ support to students who are struggling academically.
questions.explanation: Support is uncountable, and plenty of works with uncountable nouns.

questions.questionText: ___ the students were prepared, but only two achieved the highest score.
questions.explanation: All of can be followed by the determiner the and a plural noun.

questions.questionText: ___ the information in the database has been checked for accuracy.
questions.explanation: All of can refer to the whole amount of an uncountable noun.

questions.questionText: ___ the students were required to complete the practical test individually.
questions.explanation: Each of is followed by a plural noun phrase and emphasizes individuals.

questions.questionText: ___ the two candidates submitted identical proposals.
questions.explanation: Both of specifically refers to two candidates.

questions.questionText: ___ the applicants had sufficient qualifications for the position.
questions.explanation: All of can precede a determiner and plural noun.

questions.questionText: ___ of the candidates had a different response to the final question.
questions.explanation: Each of refers to members individually.

questions.questionText: The number of errors in the final report ___ unacceptable.
questions.explanation: The number of takes a singular verb.

questions.questionText: A number of errors in the final report ___ corrected before publication.
questions.explanation: A number of takes a plural verb.

questions.questionText: There were ___ mistakes in the original calculation, but the revised version is accurate.
questions.explanation: A few refers to a small number of plural countable nouns.

questions.questionText: There were ___ mistakes in the original calculation, making the result unreliable.
questions.explanation: Few emphasizes that the number of mistakes was problematic.

questions.questionText: She has ___ friends in the city, so she often feels isolated.
questions.explanation: Few indicates an insufficient number of friends.

questions.questionText: She has ___ friends in the city and can usually find someone to help her.
questions.explanation: A few means some friends are available.

questions.questionText: There is ___ chance of success unless the strategy is changed.
questions.explanation: Chance is treated as an amount in this expression, and little indicates an insufficient amount.

questions.questionText: There is ___ chance of success if we improve the strategy.
questions.explanation: A little indicates that some amount exists.

questions.questionText: The researcher did not have ___ time to verify all the results.
questions.explanation: Any is used in negative sentences with uncountable nouns.
